data.gender_notes: Marsha is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek name 'Marsia' or 'Marsos', meaning 'belonging to Mars'. In Roman mythology, Mars was the god of war and agriculture. In the Bible, a few women bear the name Marsha, including a daughter of Jethro, Moses' father-in-law. The name Marsha carries the meaning “Mars, warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Marsha usually hope their child will grow to embody mars, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marsha total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

data.cultural_impact: Marsha may conjure images of strength and determination, as the name is derived from Mars, the Roman god of war. The name has been popularized by notable figures in history, such as Marsha P. Johnson, a pioneering transgender rights activist. Marsha Bracey, a boxer, shares this name. These women, along with its ancient origins, have imbued Marsha with a sense of courage and resilience.
data.spiritual_significance: In the Christian context, the name Marsha connects us to the richly symbolic figure of Mary, the mother of Jesus. While not explicitly related to the Greek Mars, we can see the potential for further spiritual interpretation. Marsha may represent devotion and nurturing, as Mary is revered for her dedication to raising and caring for the Son of God. Alternatively, Marsha may symbolize the warrior spirit within each of us, as we strive to live our lives in accordance with God's will.
